title: Delete is a clickable div, hidden until mouse hover: not reachable by keyboard, touch or screen reader (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2)
evidence: Traced. The control is a div with no tabindex, role or accessible name, and its glyph is the only content. styles.css:12 sets .del { opacity: 0; } shown only on li:hover. The list items themselves are li elements with a click handler, also not focusable, so notes cannot be opened by keyboard either.
failing_case: Keyboard-only user: Tab goes search, New note, title, body and never reaches a note or its delete control, so no existing note can be opened or deleted. Touch user: there is no hover, so the invisible delete is a hidden tap target. Screen reader: the control is not announced.
remediation: Render each note as a real <button> for opening and a real <button aria-label="Delete note: TITLE"> for deleting. Show the delete button on :focus-within as well as :hover, and always on touch.

title: Delete is immediate with no confirm or undo, leaves the deleted note's text in the editor, and drops the active search filter
evidence: Traced. removeNote calls deleteNote and persists straight away. After deleting the open note, the title and body fields are not cleared (only the variable is). renderList() at app.js:27 is called with no argument, so the search box still has text but the list shows every note.
failing_case: The delete target is a small invisible div that appears only under the cursor. A mis-click deletes the note permanently with no undo. If the open note was deleted, the editor still shows its text as if it existed, and typing there silently fails (see the null currentNote finding). With 'foo' in the search box, deleting any note repopulates the list with all notes.
remediation: Add undo (soft delete with a timed 'Note deleted. Undo' status message) or a confirm, clear the editor, and re-render with document.getElementById('search').value.

title: Clicking a shared-note result crashes openNote and leaves currentNote undefined
evidence: Traced. Shared items are appended to #list as <li class="shared"> with no data-id (app.js:46). The delegated click handler matches any li, so Number(undefined) is NaN. openNote does notes.find(n => n.id === NaN), which gives undefined, assigns it to currentNote, and then reads currentNote.title.
failing_case: Type in the search box so /api/shared returns a result, then click it. TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined'. currentNote is now undefined, so the next edit also throws in the save timer and the previously open note's edits are not saved.
remediation: Ignore list items without a data-id (or give shared items their own handler), and make openNote return early when the note is not found.

title: maximum-scale=1 blocks pinch zoom (WCAG 1.4.4)
evidence: Read. The viewport meta disables user scaling on mobile browsers that honour it.
failing_case: A low-vision user on a phone cannot pinch-zoom the note text.

title: Title input and body textarea have no label or name; search relies on a placeholder (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2)
evidence: Read. #title and #body have no label, aria-label or placeholder. #search has only placeholder="Search notes" (line 13). The 'Changes save automatically' hint (line 21) is a plain span, so save status is never announced and not tied to the fields.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'edit multiline' for the title and body with no name. Once the user types in search, the placeholder disappears and nothing names the field.
remediation: Add visible <label for> elements (or at least aria-label), and put the save status in a role="status" element.

title: Unguarded JSON.parse and no shape check at load: corrupted or old data kills the whole app
evidence: Traced. A parse error throws at top level of store.js, so app.js never defines its handlers: New, search and list are all dead. A valid but wrong shape also breaks: '{}' gives an object with no .filter, so renderList (app.js:6) throws; a record without a title (older version) throws on n.title.toLowerCase() (app.js:6). There is no schema version on the saved value.
failing_case: localStorage.notes = '{bad' (or a half-written value, or an earlier version's records without title). Load the page: Uncaught SyntaxError or TypeError, blank list, unusable New button, and the user cannot recover without clearing site data manually.
remediation: Wrap the parse in try/catch, check Array.isArray, normalise each record (string title, string body, numeric id), keep a copy of the bad value, tell the user, and add a version field to the saved shape.

title: No flush on pagehide or unload: the last 500 ms of typing is lost on close or refresh
evidence: Traced. The only write path for edits is the debounce timer. No pagehide, beforeunload or visibilitychange handler exists in store.js or app.js. The page tells the user 'Changes save automatically' (index.html:21).
failing_case: Type a sentence into a note and press F5 or close the tab within half a second. The pending timer dies with the page, the text is gone, and the hint promised it was saved.
remediation: Add a pagehide/visibilitychange listener that cancels the timer and runs the save synchronously for the captured note.

title: Debounced save writes to whatever note is current when the timer fires, so edits overwrite another note
evidence: Traced. scheduleSave captures nothing at schedule time. The timer callback reads the global currentNote and the live DOM values 500 ms later. openNote (app.js:17-19) reassigns currentNote and replaces the DOM values synchronously, and does not flush or cancel the pending timer.
failing_case: Notes A and B exist, A is open. Type in A's body, then click B within 500 ms. openNote(B) loads B's text into the fields and sets currentNote=B. The timer then fires and writes B's own text into B (A's edit is lost, never written to A). Worse: edit A, click B, immediately type a character in B; or the reverse order with the timer from A firing after the switch, saves B's fields to B and A keeps its old text. A's typed text is silently lost every time.
remediation: Capture the note id and the field values when scheduling (or flush the pending save inside openNote before switching). One writer per record, keyed by id.

title: Failed writes (quota, private mode) are swallowed while the UI says changes save automatically
evidence: Traced. persist() catches every error from localStorage.setItem and does nothing. createNote, scheduleSave and deleteNote all call it and continue as if it worked. The hint at index.html:21 is static.
failing_case: Storage is full or disabled (Safari private mode with a quota of 0, or a note body of several MB). The user keeps typing, sees no error, closes the tab, and everything since the failure is gone. A deleted note also comes back on reload.
remediation: Have persist() return a result, show a visible and announced error with the cause and a next step ('Storage is full: export or delete notes'), and keep the in-memory state marked unsaved. Make the hint reflect the real state.

title: Fixed 1200px layout with a 300px + 1fr grid: sideways scroll at 390px and at 200% zoom
evidence: Traced. .container has a fixed width, and .layout (line 7) has a fixed 300px column with no media query anywhere in the file. At 390px the page is about 1200px wide. Combined with the zoom block in index.html:5, mobile users have no way to read it.
failing_case: Open at 390px wide: the page scrolls horizontally, the editor sits off-screen to the right. At 200% zoom on a 1360px desktop the container exceeds the viewport.
remediation: Use max-width: 1200px; width: 100%, stack .layout into one column under about 700px with a media query.

title: Focus outline removed from every control with no replacement (WCAG 2.4.7)
evidence: Read. The rule removes the default focus indicator on the button and both inputs. No :focus-visible rule or box-shadow exists elsewhere in styles.css. The text fields have only a 1px #eee border (line 13).
failing_case: Tab to New note, search, title or body: nothing changes visually, so a keyboard user cannot tell where focus is.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px; } at 3:1 against the adjacent colours.

title: Text contrast fails AA: hint #ccc on white is about 1.6:1, rank badge #bbb is about 1.9:1 (WCAG 1.4.3)
evidence: Computed from the sRGB relative luminance formula: #ccc is 1.6:1 and #bbb is 1.9:1 on #fff, against the required 4.5:1. #bbb is at styles.css:11 (#list small). White text on the #6366f1 button (line 5) is about 4.5:1 (4.47) at 14px, and the hero gradient's #8b5cf6 end is lower.
failing_case: The only save-status text and the rank badges are near invisible for low-vision users and in daylight.
remediation: Use #595959 or darker for secondary text, and a darker indigo (e.g. #4f46e5) for button and hero backgrounds.

title: Note titles and shared-note titles are written into innerHTML unescaped (stored and cross-user XSS)
evidence: Traced. renderList builds an HTML string from n.title and assigns it with list.innerHTML +=. The title comes from the #title input, saved by scheduleSave (store.js:16) and reloaded from localStorage. The search handler (app.js:46) does the same with s.title from /api/shared, which is other users' data. No escaping or textContent anywhere.
failing_case: Type in the title field, wait 500 ms, reload: the script runs on every page load. A shared note whose title is that string runs in the browser of every user who searches and gets it back.
remediation: Build list items with createElement and textContent (or escape every interpolated value in one helper). Treat /api/shared results as untrusted the same way.

quote: const sorted = notes.slice().sort((a, b) => b.updated - a.updated);
title: renderList copies and sorts all notes for every shown note and rebuilds the DOM with innerHTML += (O(n^2 log n))
evidence: Traced. Inside shown.forEach, a full sort of notes runs per item and sorted.indexOf(n) is another O(n). list.innerHTML += at line 10 re-parses the whole list every iteration. It runs on every open note, delete and search keystroke.
failing_case: 500 notes: about 500 sorts of 500 elements plus 500 re-parses of a growing list on every keystroke in the search box. At 5,000 notes it is tens of millions of operations per keystroke and the input visibly stalls.
remediation: Sort once before the loop, build a Map id to rank, and build the markup in an array joined once (or use DOM nodes appended to a fragment).

title: Search responses are appended in arrival order, never checked, and failures only go to the console
evidence: Traced. Each keystroke fires a fetch, and each response does insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend') onto the list. Nothing aborts earlier requests or checks that q is still the current value. res.ok is not tested, and the catch is console.log(e) (app.js:47). Any later renderList (openNote, removeNote, app.js:20,27) wipes the shared items.
failing_case: Type 'a' then 'b'. The slow response for 'a' arrives after the one for 'b' and is appended below it: the list shows results for both queries, with stale ones last. A 500 or an HTML 404 page makes res.json() throw and the user sees nothing at all, with no sign the shared search failed.
remediation: Render shared results in their own container, use an AbortController (or a request counter) so only the latest query applies, check res.ok, and show an inline error.

title: Notes are keyed by Date.now(), so two creates in the same millisecond share an id
evidence: Traced. createNote uses Date.now() for id. openNote, deleteNote and removeNote all find or filter by id, and the inline onclick embeds the id.
failing_case: Two createNote calls within one millisecond (a script, an automated test, a double activation of a keyboard shortcut) produce two notes with the same id. openNote always opens the first, edits to the second land in the first, and deleting either removes both.
remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a counter stored with the data.

title: Saving never re-renders the list, so renamed titles and the '#rank' badge stay stale
evidence: Traced. scheduleSave updates title and updated and persists, but never calls renderList. The list is only rebuilt on open, delete, search or New.
failing_case: Rename the open note 'Untitled' to 'Groceries'. The sidebar still says 'Untitled' and the rank badge still shows the old rank until the user searches or switches notes. Search by the new title also uses stale rendering until the next render.
remediation: After a successful save, re-render the list (or update just that row).

quote:
✨ Welcome to NoteMaster

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, your notes, supercharged.
title: Shipped placeholder copy and default AI look: lorem ipsum in the hero, 'Welcome to' heading, indigo-to-violet gradient, Inter, large hero over a tool
evidence: Read. Lorem ipsum is visible user-facing text. Also the 'Welcome to' heading with a sparkle emoji, a stock #6366f1 to #8b5cf6 gradient (styles.css:3), Inter named but never loaded (styles.css:1), and a 60px-padded hero above the app that pushes the editor below the fold on laptops.
failing_case: A user opening the app sees the words 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' as the product tagline, and has to scroll past a large banner to reach the notes.
remediation: Replace the tagline with real copy, drop the hero or shrink it to a title bar, and choose a palette and type for this product.
